A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Interact3D and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons on 10 cases in Table 2, alongside generated compositions, refinement examples and failure cases.

after.justification: v2 reports original comparisons on 150 cases, human and VLM ratings, quantitative ablations in Table 3, and additional generated results and categorized failures.

M1.justification: The generation and segmentation workflow, OBB/GeoTransformer/ICP alignment, SDF collision optimization, and VLM-driven regeneration loop remain unchanged. The new ablations evaluate existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover everyday-object pairwise and multi-object composition and describe approximately 8,300 compositional scenes. The additional test cases enlarge the sample within retained coverage; the newly listed nine categories document the existing collection rather than establish a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds MIDI to Table 2 and both qualitative comparison panels, introducing an image-conditioned scene-generation comparator. New Table 3 also evaluates ICP-only, RANSAC+ICP and GeoTransformer-only registration alternatives. Jigsaw, 2BY2, PartField and PartField+RANSAC remain represented.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 expands quantitative evaluation from 10 to 150 cases and adds human and Qwen3 assessments on a 1-to-10 scale. Appendix A.2 introduces registration-variant and refinement comparisons on 150 cases. The existing CLIP and intersection metrics, including one million Monte Carlo samples, are retained.

E4.justification: Unlike v1's illustrative refinement and failure examples, v2 adds quantitative ablations examining registration alternatives and the agentic loop in Appendix A.2/Table 3. Figure 7 also adds categorized failure analysis covering reconstruction holes, symmetry ambiguity and collision-induced divergence. Earlier case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The Monte Carlo intersection-estimation procedure is unchanged; additional averages and failure counts do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the 10-case aggregates with 150-case aggregates: Interact3D image CLIP changes from 0.8248 to 0.8236 and volume intersection, in units of 10^-3, from 3.2467 to 3.8762. These are different-sample results, not demonstrated performance regressions. New results include MIDI, human/VLM ratings of 8.33/8.57 for Interact3D, Table 3 ablations, and Figure 7's 2 reconstruction-hole, 11 symmetry and 16 collision-divergence failures.

T1.justification: The task definitions, similarity-registration objective, SDF objective and intersection definitions in Equations (1)-(5) retain their mathematical substance. Equation (2) receives a parenthesis cleanup, but no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free generate-then-compose synthesis, two-stage collision-aware composition, an interactive dataset exceeding 8,000 examples, and VLM-based geometric refinement. Expanded evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the ablations concerning ICP local minima, SDF collision control and agentic corrections, and discusses MIDI's generalization limitations. It also asserts robustness to the retained hyperparameters. Existing limitations involving fine-grained geometry, symmetry and unreliable 2D-derived spatial priors remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies inference on one NVIDIA H200 and describes nine dataset categories and approximately 10,000 candidate scenes. The abstract associates the dataset with the planned code repository. Conversely, v1's explicit 4K image-resolution specification disappears; this does not establish that the actual resolution changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MIDI, CAST, 3D-FRONT and CLIP, and sharpens its contrast with data-dependent feed-forward scene generation. The broader related-work organization and existing research positioning remain intact; CAST is cited rather than evaluated.

P1.justification: v2 corrects spelling and grammar, revises several experimental paragraphs, updates affiliation information and keywords, and inserts an ablation subsection in Appendix A. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially expanded: Table 2 gains a MIDI column and two rating rows, Table 3 is added, and Figure 7 becomes a 140-case success/failure montage. Both qualitative comparison panels gain generated-image and MIDI columns. Earlier five-case examples remain represented in Figure 10, while existing workflow, failure and multi-view figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support rests on ten quantitative cases without component ablations. v2 substantially strengthens that support through 150-case comparisons, an image-conditioned generation baseline, registration and agentic-refinement tests, and explicit failure reporting. Human-rating procedures remain underspecified, uncertainty estimates are absent, and Table 3 does not cleanly isolate SDF removal. Nevertheless, the broader comparative and diagnostic evidence resolves important weaknesses in the earlier evaluation.
